# dsh-prompt-rewrite
English · 中文

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that
optimizes the prompt you are about to send.

It adds a ✨ **Optimize prompt** control next to the composer send button.
Clicking it rewrites the c

urrent draft into a structured prompt and streams the
result into a panel above the composer, with *

*Use**, **Undo**, **Copy**, and
**Close**. Nothing is sent to the agent; the draft is only replaced

when you
click **Use**.

It runs on the model the session is already routed to (the same route the next
turn would use), and
it never writes to the Session log.
### Prompt style

The rewritten prompt can take three shapes, chosen in **Settings → General →
Prompt style**:
| Style | Output |

| `plain` (default) | One continuous, heading-free prompt. |
| `sections` | `## Role` / `## Task` /

`## Context` / `## Format` headings. |
| `role-task-goal` | `Role:` / `Task:` / `Goal:` labeled line

Context` / `## Format` headings. |
| `role-task-goal` | `Role:` / `Task:` / `Goal:` labeled lines. |

## Try a rewrite
After installation, enter a draft such as “Build a task list for my team” and click **Optimize promp
t**. Review the completed result, choose **Use** to replace the draft, or **Copy** to keep it separa
tely. **Undo** restores the draft captured when you clicked Use.
This is a suggested local walkthrough, not a recorded demo. Output depends on your session’s model a
nd selected prompt style. Rewriting calls the model and may incur provider charges; it does not send
the rewritten draft as a conversation turn.

## Market

The plugin is listed in the Stijnus market index that the desktop profile already
reads, so it appea
rs in Settings → Plugin Market next to Composer Predictions:
- `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Stijnus/dsh-composer-predictions/main/market-index.json`

This repository also publishes its own format-1 index, for anyone who wants a
focused source:
- `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Stijnus/dsh-prompt-optimizer/main/market-index.json`

Market sources are cached for 10 minutes per URL by the Host, so a newly
published version can take
that long to show up in an open market panel.
## Where the rewrite logic lives

This plugin does **not** re-implement prompt rewriting. It imports the engine
from the published **P

rompt Optimizer** implementation,
`oss-prompt-optimizer`.

| Meta-prompt builder | `oss-prompt-optimizer/lib/meta.js` | `buildOptimizePrompt(input, language, e
xtraInstructions, examples, outputStyle, metaLanguage, diagnosis, templates, context, taskType, maxO

utputTokens, profile, level, builtinExamples, compact, sceneRefEnabled)` |
| Template data | `oss-pr

ompt-optimizer/lib/templates.js` | `META_PROMPT`, `META_PROMPT_EN`, `DEFAULT_TEMPLATES` |
| System-p
rompt wrapper | `oss-prompt-optimizer/lib/prompt.js` | `buildOptimizeSystem(ctx, input, outputLangua

ge, diagnosis, profile)` |
| Rewrite executor (full service) | `oss-prompt-optimizer/lib/optimizer.j

s` | `class PromptOptimizerService`, `optimize(rawInput, options)` |
| Output validation | `oss-prom
pt-optimizer/lib/validate.js` | `REQUIRED_SECTIONS`, `hasValidSections`, `truncateInput`, … |
